purpose: HD-2D casting scene art direction references

variants.name: 01-violet-storm
variants.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Generate one standalone landscape bitmap game art reference, 16:9 composition, no collage, no labels, no UI, no text, no watermark. Authentic premium HD-2D: deliberately chunky hand-authored 2D pixel sprite characters with clearly visible square pixel clusters, limited hue-shifted sprite ramps, crisp stair-step silhouettes, set in a richly textured miniature three-dimensional game environment. Strong foreground/midground/background depth, atmospheric perspective, restrained tilt-shift depth of field only away from the action; main sprite and spell perfectly legible. NOT smooth anime illustration, NOT a photograph, NOT voxel characters, NOT merely a pixel filter over a painting. Capture the peak of a powerful spell being cast: anticipation in stance, readable caster-to-target direction, large designed spell silhouette, bright core and saturated secondary shapes, sparks/debris and bounce light on the scenery. Character roughly 15-20% of image height, environment and spell the main focus. Professional production art-direction reference suitable for an RPG. Direction: ominous cold violet rainstorm and ruined observatory. A scarlet-cloaked pixel mage in the lower-left midground thrusts an illuminated staff toward a training effigy on the right. A monumental swirling celestial sigil above opens and sends a thick branching lavender-white lightning column into the target; pixel electric arcs fan across the wet basalt floor. Broken stone columns, ivy, distant layered arches, a fragmented moon and turbulent indigo clouds. Wet reflective flagstones with spell reflections, warm amber braziers at the sides contrasting the midnight blue-violet palette. Dramatic three-quarter side-view miniature diorama; strong readable pixel caster. Spell is spectacular and architectural in scale, but preserve the silhouettes and shadowy environment.
